rationale: Pages 209 and 251 describe an insulinoma evaluation with visual history and a suspected grapefruit–medication interaction with acute visual and auditory hallucinations. They are separate members and neither compares dried-fig intake in Parkinson disease.

The 20 autopsy cases include eight Lewy body dementia cases. Visual hallucinations were once only in 2/8 vs 1/12 and persistent in 4/8 vs 5/12. The authors report no significant group difference. The study does not compare food exposure or count repeated episodes.

Eye tracking during image viewing measures fixations and saccades. Visual hallucinations occur in discussion of other cannabis-related studies. The participants and measured outcome do not fit the Parkinson dried-fig comparison. FIG labels name illustrations.

Poster P64 uses visual symptoms as background to a head-drop case. Poster P102 reports psychiatric outcomes after subthalamic stimulation in eight Parkinson cases without a separately coded visual episode rate. No member provided a dried-fig comparison.
